requirements.accept: actor wrapper is an executable regular file whose bytes are revalidated immediately before actor start
configuration, wrapper, immutable inputs, output roots, and lock path reject a symlink at the named path or any existing ancestor before canonical resolution
wrapper/model/workload/runtime-config/policy paths are mutually outside state/evidence/operations and frozen production trees
the model file subjected to small_model_max_bytes is the same digest-bound path present in every model-bearing correctness, attribution, and throughput argv
factory resolves a typed lease adapter bound to mi210_0, the configured inference-window lock, allowed_discovery_noise, model byte cap, and promotion_claim=false
environment profile has an exact allowlist, rejects LD_PRELOAD/PYTHONPATH/library injection, and producer independently pins each arm LD_LIBRARY_PATH
registry dispatch entry is a typed DispatchContract whose exact/forbidden/invariant geometry is bound into the evidence policy; arbitrary mappings are refused
typed runner args bind candidate and anchor builds, actual model, workload, runtime config, contained fresh output, small-model cap, and nonpromotable discovery mode

live launch derives state_root, evidence_root, operations_root, max_iterations, nomination_threshold, device, model cap, and lock from the sealed deployment; duplicate CLI values are absent or exact-compared and refused on any mismatch

materializer rejects a SourcePatchManifest before mutation/build unless every changed path and declared symbol is in the explicit kernel-source allowlist; tools/llama-bench, benchmark/result parsers, CMake/toolchains, evaluators/profilers, tests, models, runtime configs, recipes, and measurement artifacts are forbidden

anchor and candidate preserve identical benchmark executable, runner, parser, profiler, model, workload, runtime config, toolchain, and evaluation bytes; only the candidate kernel source/build identity and linked candidate kernel DSO may differ
one typed registry value shape is accepted by both registry resolution and concrete materialization, and an end-to-end no-hardware dry launch exercises that exact public path

the live factory constructs both Codex actors from the digest-bound executable wrapper and exact allowlisted environment profile; arbitrary injected planner or critic objects cannot enter the live deployment entrypoint

the deployed command needs only the sealed deployment path and dry-run selection; registry, actors, executors, journals, claims, and callbacks come from a static trusted factory rather than caller injection

every lease, device, model-cap, overlap-mode, workload, and inference-window field checked by the factory is consumed by the actual runner rather than being an ignored Namespace attribute or module-global default

the evidence plan binds the exact deployment model, workload, runtime config, policy, dispatch contract, device, per-arm environment, required argv paths, and byte digests before any correctness or profiler child starts

the production snapshot contains the complete required frozen source, executable, HIP library, build config, linkage, branch/head, and clean-tree identities; one arbitrary bound file cannot satisfy the snapshot contract
the first planner turn receives a digest-bound workload and bounded source/hotspot/profile context plus source-scope constraints, so it can select an informed kernel hypothesis without hidden state

later planner turns receive a typed projection of measured effect, classification, evidence hashes, dispatch proof, correctness proof, and do-not-repeat disposition; opaque result hashes alone are insufficient

the actor prompt supplies bounded sealed source excerpts, the complete output schema/template, and controller-assigned campaign/proposal/candidate/base/instrument IDs; the model authors only hypothesis, bounded source change, falsifier, and diff, and its output round-trips through manifest and source-scope validation

deployment pins a versioned allowlisted correctness/dispatch template registry rather than one fixed dispatch contract; each planner candidate selects a typed template and bounded hotspot intent, the critic reviews it, manifest paths and symbols deterministically match it, and evidence resolves commands and geometry without accepting actor-authored argv or regex

one autonomous controller run can screen two sequential candidates selecting different sealed templates and hotspots, while each operation and resume checkpoint retains the exact selected template version and intent identity
